answer: That makes each additional alias in a cluster strictly dilutive, so the operator pays the bond and the voyage fee for a smaller payout than one honest position would earn. Because the violet cluster is derived from funding history, the split is applied at settlement and the nectar audit lists each share. The reward pool is divided per detected cluster rather than per key, so 141 linked identities split one share instead of collecting 141 of them. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
